subject: [URGENT] client-visible silent chunks & chunked-transfer timeouts — BrightLeaf impact
messages:
From: Gina Morales <gina@brightleaf.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightLeaf Platform <ops@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent silent chunks during high throughput - urgent

Karthik —

We started a staged rollout of our streaming assistant feature at ~09:00 PT and by ~09:15 we began seeing intermittent periods where clients get a long silence (no chunks) even though the connection remains open. The client-side logs show chunk boundaries but no payload for several seconds; some sessions then end with 502/504 from our NGINX edge. Impact: ~3-6% of sessions in the canary group experienced partial responses or disconnects, which is causing retries and duplicated actions in the product.

We captured a few request IDs and included a debug bundle (brightleaf_debug_20280330.tar.gz). Sample IDs: req-20280330-7341, req-20280330-7399. You can see spikes in the attached Grafana link around 09:18.

This is customer-facing and blocking our rollout. Can you escalate and tell us: (1) whether this is a Redwood runtime issue vs our proxy config; (2) an ETA for an initial mitigation; (3) will this require an immediate rollback?

We'd like a VIP war room and exec sync if this persists.

Thanks,
Gina Morales
Director, Platform Engineering — BrightLeaf

Attachments: brightleaf_debug_20280330.tar.gz (attachment)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Gina Morales <gina@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, BrightLeaf Platform <ops@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent silent chunks during high throughput - urgent

Gina — thanks for the heads up and the bundle. We received the archive and I've triaged the initial signals. Quick answers up front: we haven't seen a global outage, this appears related to a specific traffic/size pattern hitting the streaming path. We've spun up a small triage loop and will propose mitigations in the next 90 minutes.

Questions for you that speed diagnosis:
- Are these sessions hitting our Hosted API endpoints (us-west-2) or your Dedicated cluster?
- Any configuration on your NGINX front-door (proxy_buffering off/on, upstream timeouts)?
- Do you see the same behavior for short-context requests?

Preliminary hypotheses:
- NGINX / edge proxy upstream timeout + proxy_buffering causing chunk coalescing under burst.
- Worker-side transient stall (GC or CUDA NVLink saturation) causing delayed chunk flush.
- Socket keepalive/heartbeat mismatch between client/front-proxy and backend.

I'm looping in Marissa and Stephanie to run live checks on the runtime and to look at the request IDs you provided. Can we do a 30m war room at 10:15 PT (I can host)?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Gina Morales <gina@brightleaf.ai>, BrightLeaf Platform <ops@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: ACTION: live triage — BrightLeaf silent chunk incidents (req-20280330-*)

Team —

Forwarding Gina's note and the debug bundle. This is an enterprise canary (deal HB-4921). Need immediate triage and a clear mitigation plan for Gina. Please treat as P1 for the next 4 hours.

Ask: Can you run the following ASAP and report back in the war room at 10:15 PT?
1) Check frontend NGINX access + error logs for upstream timeouts and proxy_buffering behavior at 09:10–09:30.
2) Correlate the provided request IDs to worker logs (trace IDs, GC pause, NVLink / GPU kernel stalls).
3) Verify socket-level metrics (send/recv buffers) — are chunks being emitted then dropped by the proxy?
4) Prepare a short list of mitigations (canary config change, heartbeat frequency change, route to fallback model) and estimated time-to-fix.

We may need a dedicated canary rollback option; Gina has asked for exec visibility if this persists. I'll prepare the exec brief once we have techno-scope.

Thanks — K
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Gina Morales <gina@brightleaf.ai>, BrightLeaf Platform <ops@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACTION: live triage — BrightLeaf silent chunk incidents (req-20280330-*)

Quick update from runtime triage (notes):
- Correlated req-20280330-7341 and req-20280330-7399 to worker span ids. At ~09:18 PT we observe a ~4.8s pause inside the inference loop on a subset of workers. CPU and GPU stack traces show NVLink contention and long kernel queue times when large-context (>8k tokens) requests hit at high QPS.
- NGINX logs show repeated "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)" for several upstreams at 09:18 with the default proxy_read_timeout at 30s. We also found proxy_buffering was enabled in the edge config for that host which can coalesce chunks and delay delivery until buffers are filled.
- The combination means: worker stalls cause delayed chunk emission; proxy buffering holds incomplete chunks, client sees silence; eventually proxy times out or client retries.

Suggested mitigation (short-term):
1) Set proxy_buffering off for the BrightLeaf host at the edge (canary first) — immediate effect on chunk delivery. (estimate: 20m to canary, 1h to roll to prod)
2) Increase proxy_read_timeout to 90s to avoid mid-request timeouts while we stabilize. (estimate: 10m)
3) Enable a runtime override that forces chunk flush after N millis when GPU queue latency exceeds threshold (engine change). (estimate: 6h for hotfix + canary)
4) As an operational fallback, route BrightLeaf canary traffic to a lower-concurrency pool (reduce NVLink contension) — may increase cost but reduces error rate. (estimate: 30m to switch)

Attachments: nginx_fix_patch.diff (edge config snippet), support_manifest_0303.json (collected metrics).

I'll prepare an exec one-pager. If you want me to push the proxy_buffering off now to the canary, say the word and I'll coordinate with edge infra.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Gina Morales <gina@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, BrightLeaf Platform <ops@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent silent chunks during high throughput - urgent

Gina —

Thanks for your patience. Engineering confirmed the root-candidate (proxy_buffering + worker stalls under large-context bursts). Recommended immediate steps:
- We'll flip proxy_buffering off for your canary tonight at 00:30 PT (canary window) and monitor.
- Bump proxy_read_timeout to 90s during the rollout window.
- If you prefer, we can route your canary to a lower-concurrency pool for the next 24 hours to reduce risk.

We're also preparing a runtime hotfix to force chunk flush when kernel latencies spike; ETA ~6h for canary.

As an immediate customer gesture, we will issue a credit for the hours of disruption and prioritize the hotfix. Please confirm if you want the canary change tonight or prefer an immediate rollback.

I'll schedule an exec sync at 16:00 PT if this continues.

—Karthik
